packs.title: First little conversations
packs.description: Requests, updates, and everyday moments at work.

lessons.en: I am sending you the dashboard.
lessons.title: Send a dashboard

words.note: A familiar English loanword.
전달 드립니다 is a polite way to say you are sending something.

lessons.en: I’ll send you the materials by tomorrow morning.
lessons.title: By tomorrow morning

words.note: A useful time word.
오전 means morning; 까지 marks the deadline here.
자료 means materials or data; 를 marks the object.
A respectful promise to send something. The base verb is 보내다.

lessons.en: I will let you know once the work is done.
lessons.title: When the work is done

words.note: The task you are working on.
완료 means completion. 되면 adds “when it becomes / is done”.
A respectful way to say you will tell someone.

lessons.en: The analysis takes a little while.
lessons.title: It takes a little time

words.note: 이 marks 분석 as the subject here.
Often also softens what you are saying.
걸리다 can mean “to take” when talking about time.

lessons.en: Thank you for your kind help.
lessons.title: Thank someone for their help

words.note: 친절하다 describes being kind.
Related to 돕다, “to help”.
A respectful workplace expression of thanks.

lessons.en: I will contact you as soon as possible.
lessons.title: Get back to someone

words.note: These words form a useful phrase together.
연락드리겠습니다 politely promises future contact.

lessons.en: Ah, I'll fix this
lessons.title: Fix something

words.note: Conversational form of 이것.
해보겠습니다 means “I will try doing it”.

lessons.en: Thank you, even though it's late.
lessons.title: Thanks, even this late

words.note: 늦다 describes being late.
늦은 시간 means “a late hour”.

lessons.en: Deletion is complete.
lessons.title: Confirm completion

words.note: Used for removing a file, record or entry.
하였습니다 is a formal past-tense form of 하다, “to do”.

lessons.en: The service code stays the same.
lessons.title: Something stays the same

words.note: 코드 is “code”; 는 marks the topic.
그대로 means “unchanged / as it is”.

lessons.en: This meeting will be held in English.
lessons.title: A meeting in English

words.note: 미팅 is a loanword; 은 marks the topic.
영어 means English; 로 indicates the language here.
A common formal expression for how an event is run.

lessons.en: Please check the inquiry above.
lessons.title: Ask someone to check

words.note: 의 connects 위, “above”, to the following noun.
A common word in work messages.
A useful request phrase. The export uses spaces in 드립니다.

lessons.en: Hello, I'm sending the document number.
lessons.title: Send a document number

words.note: 문서번호 combines “document” and “number”.
Used for identifiers, phone numbers and document numbers.
The same polite phrase as 전달 드립니다, written together.

lessons.en: I am sending it attached.
lessons.title: Send an attachment

words.note: Common in emails with an attached file.
A formal connective form of 하다, “to do”.

lessons.en: Here is my answer to the matters you inquired about.
lessons.title: Reply to an inquiry

words.note: 주신 politely refers to the other person making the inquiry.
A general workplace word for a point or matter.
답변드립니다 is a polite way to introduce your reply.

lessons.ko: 이 쿼리에 대한 접근 권한 부탁드립니다
lessons.en: Please grant me access to this query.
lessons.title: Ask for access

words.note: A familiar data / database loanword.
Connects a noun to the thing it concerns.
접근 means access; 권한 means permission or authority.

lessons.ko: 해당 오류 해결 방법 확인 부탁드립니다
lessons.en: Please check how to resolve this error.
lessons.title: Ask how to resolve an error

words.note: Used for system, data or process errors.
해결 방법 is a method of resolving something.
A building-block word in instructions and questions.

lessons.en: Please apply them one at a time.
lessons.title: One at a time

words.note: 한 is “one”; 번 counts occasions; 에 indicates the time.
씩 distributes a quantity: one each.
적용 means application; 해 주세요 makes a polite request.

lessons.en: In which table was it changed?
lessons.title: Which table changed?

words.note: Asks which one among alternatives.
테이블 means table; 에서 marks the place of an action.
변경 means change. 되었나요 asks politely about a past change.

lessons.en: Revenue is an estimate that includes all subsidies.
lessons.title: Understand an estimate

words.note: 은 marks the topic in this sentence.
모든 means all; 을 marks the object.
추정 is estimation; 액 is an amount of money.

lessons.en: Reduce unnecessary costs.
lessons.title: Reduce costs

words.note: 불필요하다 means “to be unnecessary”.
을 marks the thing being reduced.
Plain written form of 줄이다, suitable for notes and plans; not a polite request.

lessons.en: After checking, I will issue it and send it to you.
lessons.title: Check, then send

chunks.en: I will send it to you

words.note: Follows an action noun: 확인 후, “after checking”.
Used for issuing documents or certificates.

words.en: I will do it for you
words.note: A respectful ending used in promises and offers.

lessons.en: It would be good to get your opinions.
lessons.title: Ask for opinions

chunks.en: I think that would be good

words.note: Useful in meetings and feedback requests.
A polite conditional form of 주다.
Softens an opinion or suggestion.

lessons.ko: 이슈 상품 리스트 혹시 공유 가능하실까요?
lessons.en: Could you possibly share the list of issue products?
lessons.title: Ask for a list

words.note: A common word throughout your work.
Makes a request less direct.

words.en: would it be possible for you to share?
words.note: 공유 means sharing; 가능 means possibility.

lessons.ko: 제가 잘못 이해한 부분이 있다면 말씀 부탁드립니다
lessons.en: If there is anything I misunderstood, please tell me
lessons.title: Check your understanding

chunks.en: if there is anything I misunderstood

words.note: The humble form 저 with subject marker 가.
잘못 means wrongly; 이해 means understanding.
A conditional form of 있다.

packs.description: Offline voices for words, pasted text, Voice B, and custom lessons.
